blocks.text: JR100 is a high-G recovery data recorder designed specifically for **aircraft, UAVs and other demanding applications**. It provides **{{ models.main.shock_overload }} shock resistance**, tolerance of flight vibration and stable operation across **{{ models.main.operating_temperature }}**.

Applications include flight tests, high-G and recovery tests, and integration with telemetry and data-acquisition systems. JR100 stores received serial and Ethernet data locally for retrieval after recovery, supporting test review, operating-history analysis and fault investigation.

Landing and recovery can produce severe shock loads, while sustained flight vibration and temperature changes also challenge recording equipment. JR100 treats these conditions as design inputs, carrying reliability requirements through **system architecture, component selection, mechanical optimization, software reliability, application-specific testing and flight validation**.

System design addresses task conditions, and component choices reflect environmental and reliability requirements. Targeted mechanical and software optimization is evaluated through testing and actual flight trials. From analysis and engineering design to practical validation, this process strengthens **reliability, robustness and operational stability**.

Backed by extensive engineering experience, **JR100 has successfully completed data-recording tasks in multiple flight tests**, supporting post-test review and analysis. This experience also informs airborne system integration, test coordination, post-recovery retrieval and product selection.

items: **Multi-source recording:** receive serial and Ethernet data and store test data locally for post-recovery analysis and traceability.
**Isolated interfaces and low-power design:** isolated RS-422, Ethernet and power connections support integration with airborne telemetry systems.
**Application-specific software:** software can be adapted to customer requirements for data protocols, recording control, status monitoring and data retrieval to fit the test workflow.

blocks.text: These parameters describe environmental capabilities and interface performance. Ethernet interface rate is not a sustained storage or export rate. Recording performance depends on the data load and delivered configuration.

Software can be customized for customer requirements, including protocol adaptation, recording control, status monitoring, file management and data retrieval. Communication formats, feedback behavior and operating workflows are agreed per project rather than fixed by a particular software version.

Provide shock conditions, vibration spectrum, installation requirements, data rates and recording duration to confirm storage capacity, software requirements and the delivered configuration. Shock pulse duration, direction and other environmental conditions can be clarified during project integration.
